gen-gf-jim-nightshade-satoshi: Smudgy and loose: Jim Nightshade packs its handwritten letters into a dark texture, while Satoshi stays generous with a soaring x-height. Jim Nightshade wins quick phrases; Satoshi handles all the rest.
gen-gf-jim-nightshade-switzer: Scribbled and snug, Jim Nightshade crowds its casual letters into a dark, blurry texture with no stroke contrast at all. Switzer, a tubular sans, keeps going smoothly, though a couple of lines is where the pair feels best.
gen-gf-julee-archivo: Archivo flares its curves outward and stands on a commanding x-height, a plain sans with real presence. And Julee supplies the charm, its tightly pressed, cable-thick handwriting doing its best work in brief lines, not long paragraphs.
gen-gf-julee-fs-asap: Julee presses its letters together in a friendly, hand-drawn crowd, with no brush-style swell anywhere. And Asap, its arcs open and its lowercase nearly capital height, supplies the readability Julee lacks across long paragraphs.
gen-gf-julee-fs-epilogue: Julee crowds its handwritten letters together like bundled cable. Epilogue loosens everything, with curvy, wire-like monoline strokes and stubby ascenders, so it takes the longer text while Julee stays with short lines.
gen-gf-julee-fs-erode: Julee is friendly handwriting with no brush-like pressure swell, its letters packed in narrow channels of space. Erode adds a faint nib-pressure ebb and flow and dignified editorial polish, ideal for a couple of lines.
gen-gf-julee-general-sans: General Sans keeps a steady pen pressure from first letter to last, with an x-height that fills the line. Julee stays with a few lines; this sans flows on smoothly beyond them.
gen-gf-julee-switzer: Crisp and wire-like, with c tips that never drift toward touching, this Swiss-leaning sans reads cleanly. Switzer sits against Julee, whose packed handwriting wants a quick line of words rather than pages.
gen-gf-julee-work-sans: Julee presses friendly, hand-drawn letters into narrow channels, while Work Sans keeps its c tips apart. One packs tight, the other opens up; short lines work best.
gen-gf-kablammo-fs-paquito: Paquito reads confident and approachable, its lowercase sitting close to the caps, while Kablammo sets a deliberate pace with wide spacing. Kablammo leads loudly, Paquito follows quietly; a few lines is plenty.
